title: Ex 2.5 #2 · Truth table for (Q ∨ R) ⇔ (R ∧ Q)
prompt: Build a truth table for $(Q \vee R) \Leftrightarrow (R \wedge Q)$ and enter the truth value of the whole statement in each row.
answer_format: Four T/F values, one per row, top to bottom, like T F T T. Rows (Q, R) go TT, TF, FT, FF, as in the book. Helper columns are optional steps, like ~Q : F F T T.
hints: Only the letters Q and R appear, so the table has four rows.
Make helper columns for Q ∨ R and R ∧ Q. A ⇔ statement is true exactly when its two sides have the same truth value, including when both are false.
solution: The helper columns are $Q \vee R$: T T T F and $R \wedge Q$: T F F F.
The two sides agree in the first row (both true) and the last row (both false), and disagree in the middle two rows.
So the column is T F F T.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).

steps.content: Q ∨ R : T T T F
R ∧ Q : T F F F
